title: Maybe Catch a Spark
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Taking its title from a line in the film A Complete Unknown, where a young Bob Dylan visits Woody Guthrie hoping to 'maybe catch a spark,' this essay argues creative insight is rarely spontaneous — it's the product of deliberately exposing oneself to stimulating people, places, and experiences. It contends creative thinkers intentionally seek out conversations, artwork, unfamiliar environments, and cutting-edge practitioners specifically to trigger new thinking, and that the odds of a breakthrough rise the more novel the stimulus. The piece closes by encouraging readers to treat 'spark-hunting' as an intentional practice rather than something that only happens by chance.
points: Uses the Dylan/Guthrie scene from A Complete Unknown as a narrative frame for the concept of deliberately seeking creative catalysts.
Argues insight is rarely purely spontaneous — it results from intentional exposure to varied, high-energy stimuli.
Claims proximity to other creative or high-talent people is one of the most reliable ways to trigger new thinking.
Frames 'catching a spark' as a repeatable, intentional practice rather than a passive hope.
Positions surprise as the essential ingredient of the creative process, achieved by seeking out unfamiliar people and environments.
quotes: Seeger is not insulted when Dylan focuses his adulation and attention on Guthrie. But Seeger is curious and asks him why he was so intent on meeting Guthrie. Dylan replies that he wanted to meet Woody to “maybe catch a spark.
Regardless, creative thinkers, strategists, and designers intentionally expose themselves to a variety of stimuli, hoping for just such a spark.
The very idea of intentionally looking to “catch a spark” is an important step for artists, thinkers, and leaders. You can’t find what you aren’t looking for.
By engaging others with high talent for creative expression, it’s possible they will say or do something that sets off the chain reaction of imaginative thinking.
Make it an intentional process, and you’ll be more likely to find a connection you weren’t thinking of. At the heart of creativity is surprise.
